correction_1_the_worker_program_does_exi.measured_now: The registry's argv is relative to the fork, not the repo root: third_party/mu/packages/coding-agent exists, and its package.json defines build:unbundled = 'tsgo -p tsconfig.build.json && shx chmod +x dist/cli.js dist/rpc-entry.js && npm run copy-assets', with bin pi -> dist/bundle/cli.js. The root package.json build script compiles chord, tui, telemetry, ai, durable, agent, session-backends/sqlite-node, protocol, client, server and then coding-agent. So the entry is a build artifact that has never been produced here: at the time of writing, third_party/mu/packages/coding-agent/dist is absent and third_party/mu/node_modules is absent, meaning fork.install_deps and fork.build_worker were never run.
correction_1_the_worker_program_does_exi.what_i_started: fork.install_deps and fork.build_worker are UNBOUND, so their documented commands were run directly with the pinned toolchain (C:/nvm4w/nodejs/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js, sha 3ce7cba6..., npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund then npm run build in third_party/mu). The run is logged to .local/mu_npm_ci.log and its outcome is NOT claimed here; record the rc and the produced dist listing when it finishes, and if it fails on the network say so instead of calling the worker available.

correction_2_what_is_still_genuinely_mis.the_claim_that_survives: Nothing in the product tree serves the broker's HTTP envelope. internal/domain/runtime_broker_windows.go:31 declares Endpoint, :78 parses it and :183-194 POSTs {key, epoch, run_id, capability, payload} with an Idempotency-Key and a bearer token, but git grep -l ListenAndServe over tracked files returns only ops/remote_access/gateway/main.go plus two copies under execution/verifier. adapters/runtime is worker admission and isolation (dispatch_key, epoch >= 1, sandbox profile appcontainer-zero-capabilities-v1, adapter_revision, journal/lease/wall deadline, CODEX_HOME environment) with no listener and no exec.Command/StdinPipe.
correction_2_what_is_still_genuinely_mis.the_open_question: coding-agent's rpc-entry.js is a JSON-RPC CLI entry, while the broker speaks HTTP POST. Whether the built worker can be reached as a provider endpoint at all - directly, or through a bridge that translates the envelope to the RPC pipe - is unproven, and it is the actual thing between W14-01 and a LIVE run. Do not treat 'the file will exist after build' as 'the cycle will run'.
correction_2_what_is_still_genuinely_mis.registry_defect_found_by_a_previous_wind: execution/v2.4/registry_binding_readiness_notes.md records that fork.worker_stop's argv is just ['--stop'] with executable node and cwd '.', which cannot run as written, and that its owner is the already-ACCEPTED W05-01. I did not verify that independently in this window; it is cited, not confirmed.
